newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: EL SALVADOR SEES GRAIN CROP DOWN 12 PCT ON EL NINO.
newsitem.headline: EL SALVADOR SEES GRAIN CROP DOWN 12 PCT ON EL NINO.

text.p: El Salvador's government said Tuesday that the lack of rains stemming from this year's El Nino weather system would hit the country's grains harvest by 10 to 12 percent.
The Agriculture Ministry said the 1997-1998 grains harvest, originally forecast at 22.1 million quintals (100-lb bags), will be down 10 to 12 percent because of the rainfall shortage.

Agriculture Minister Ricardo Quinonez said the government will facilitate imports of 1.5 million quintals of corn and dry beans for human destined for consumption because of foreseen shortages from March next year.
Imports will be done via private sector grains houses, he added.

The government is studying measures to alleviate the effect of El Nino, a weather system that warms seas off the South American Pacific coast and throws global patterns into turmoil. Financial aid to farmers is on the table, government sources said.

El Salvador's Morazan, La Union, San Miguel and Usulutan regions are most affected by the lack of rain. One report from the Morazan region had crop damage calculated at 70 percent of the corn and dry beans planted.
